key_insight: SMI turns each medical concept into an ontology-based coarse-to-fine semantic path and uses it to build hierarchy-aware representations that are especially helpful for rare, fine-grained codes.
clinical_relevance: This could improve downstream clinical prediction and recommendation by making biomedical models better reflect medical hierarchies instead of treating codes as unrelated labels.
method: Define each diagnosis, procedure, or medication as a Semantic ID from an expert ontology path
Aggregate frozen biomedical LM embeddings across ontology levels to create concept representations
Optionally learn level weights on validation data for a weighted variant
evidence_signal: Evaluations on MIMIC-IV and eICU show improved mortality, readmission, drug recommendation, rare drug prediction, and better robustness under cross-hospital shift.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the underlying medical ontology, and validation-tuned level weights may not transfer equally well across institutions or coding systems.
paper_title: SMI: Ontology-Grounded Semantic IDs for Hierarchy-Aware Medical Concept Representation
